rows.grounds: compound: one who abandons my grace

items.question: What consequence follows for one who abandons divine grace?
premises: A person may abandon divine grace
Divine grace is something to be received
Worthiness depends on acceptance of grace
items.inference: One who abandons divine grace does not deserve to receive it.
items.plain_english: One who abandons my grace does not deserve my grace.

rows.grounds: fused form with ca and eva
expresses obligation or possibility of giving

items.question: How may the consecrated grace-gift be given to wives and disciples?
premises: The grace-gift is consecrated
Wives and disciples are potential recipients
Giving requires proper manner
items.inference: The manner of giving the grace-gift to wives and disciples must be clarified.
items.plain_english: And how is the grace-gift to be given to wives and to disciples?

rows.grounds: compound listing purificatory acts beginning with mouth-rinsing

items.question: How can acts like mouth-rinsing purification be properly accomplished?
premises: Purificatory acts such as mouth-rinsing are required
These acts must be properly performed
Their proper accomplishment is in question
items.inference: The proper way to accomplish mouth-rinsing and similar purifications must be explained.
items.plain_english: How may mouth-rinsing, purification, and such acts be properly accomplished?

rows.grounds: reason for the question about mouth-purity

items.question: How can mouth purification occur given the inherent purity of divine grace?
premises: Divine grace is inherently pure
Mouth purification is ordinarily required
Purity of grace raises a question about further purification
items.inference: The need or manner of mouth purification must be reconciled with the purity of grace.
items.plain_english: Since the grace is pure, how can there be purification of the mouth?

rows.grounds: refers to what has been offered
refers to the act or situation in question

items.question: How can proper procedure be maintained if the grace has already been offered?
premises: The grace may already be offered
Ritual procedure must remain proper
Prior offering raises a procedural question
items.inference: The compatibility of prior offering with proper procedure must be explained.
items.plain_english: If it has already been offered, how can that be properly accomplished?

rows.grounds: compound referring to all preceding questions
request to declare or make known
imperative request for deliverance from doubt

items.question: Why must all these doubts be explained to uplift the community of devotees?
premises: Several doubts have been raised
Devotees require clear guidance
Explanation can remove confusion
items.inference: Explaining all these matters is necessary to uplift the devotees.
items.plain_english: Having explained all this, uplift the host of devotees.

rows.grounds: means by which fault is avoided
compound: fault of abandoning what was offered

items.question: Does giving away what was offered constitute a fault of abandonment?
premises: Something offered may be given to others
Abandonment of the offered could be seen as a fault
Giving is a deliberate transfer
items.inference: There is no fault of abandoning the offered when it is given.
items.plain_english: O lady, by giving it, there is no fault of abandoning what was offered.

rows.grounds: compound: abandonment not done according to rule

items.question: Can abandonment outside formal ritual procedure be free of fault and even virtuous?
premises: Abandonment may occur outside formal ritual
Fault is usually associated with improper abandonment
Context can determine moral value
items.inference: Such abandonment is not a fault but indeed a virtue.
items.plain_english: Just as abandonment not done according to ritual rule is not a fault, it is indeed a virtue.

items.question: Does performing necessary acts in this manner avoid ritual taint?
premises: Various acts must be performed
Performance can be done in a proper manner
Proper performance affects purity
items.inference: One who performs those acts in this way is not tainted.
items.plain_english: Those various acts indeed must be done; doing them thus, one is not tainted.

items.question: Is abandonment compelled by necessity considered a rule-based fault?
premises: Abandonment may occur under compulsion
Faults are often defined by ritual rules
Compulsion affects culpability
items.inference: Forced abandonment in that context is not a rule-based fault.
items.plain_english: In that case, abandonment done under compulsion is not a fault grounded in rule.

rows.grounds: compound giving reason for no loss of purity
fused form denying loss or need in that way
denies that purification is sought or required

items.question: Why is additional purification not required when there is no contact with saliva?
premises: Impurity may arise from saliva contact
In this case there is no such contact
Purification is required only when impurity occurs
items.inference: Because there is no saliva contact, additional purification is not required.
uncertainties: The exact force of the double negation in śuddhirna na hīṣyate is slightly ambiguous.
items.plain_english: Because there is no contact with saliva, purity is not lost there and no further purification is required.

rows.grounds: compound describing one engaged in contemplating my name
compound referring to other deities and such

items.question: Should one intent on contemplating the divine name remember other deities?
premises: A devotee may be intent on contemplating the divine name
Remembrance can be directed to various deities
Exclusive focus is a devotional claim
items.inference: One intent on contemplating my name should not remember other deities.
items.plain_english: One intent on contemplating my name should not remember other gods and such.

rows.grounds: compound describing agents devoted solely to you
fused form: those acts are to be done

items.question: How should those supremely devoted to the Lord alone perform required acts?
premises: Some devotees are devoted to the Lord alone
Certain acts must still be performed
Exclusive devotion raises questions about practice
items.inference: The manner in which exclusively devoted practitioners should perform those acts must be clarified.
items.plain_english: O Lord, how are those acts to be done by those who are supremely devoted to you alone?

rows.grounds: compound with ca: service or use of that mantra

items.question: Does a servant become tainted by engaging in service involving that mantra?
premises: A servant may engage in service involving that mantra
Such service could be suspected of causing taint
Devotional service is evaluated by rule
items.inference: The servant is not tainted by that mantra-service.
uncertainties: The precise scope of tanmantryādeḥ (mantra, command, or service) is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: And the servant is not tainted by service involving that mantra.

rows.grounds: compound referring to regular and occasional rites

items.question: Does service to another deity in daily or occasional rites cause taint?
premises: Daily and occasional rites may involve service
Service to another deity may occur in such rites
Such service could be thought to cause taint
items.inference: Service to another deity in daily and occasional rites does not cause taint.
items.plain_english: And in daily and occasional rites, service to another deity does not cause taint.

rows.grounds: fused verb and recipient: give to non-devotees

items.question: To whom must the consecrated offering not be given under any circumstances?
premises: The offering may be distributed

Distribution is subject to restriction
items.inference: One should not give it to non-devotees or to those of another kind.
uncertainties: The exact sense of vijātīyebhyaḥ depends on ritual and social context.
items.plain_english: One should not give it to non-devotees, nor indeed to those of another kind.

rows.grounds: mental attitude toward the offering or recipient
refers to the one who considers it low
fused form stating devotion is fruitless

items.question: What happens to devotion when one regards the sacred offering as low?
premises: A person may regard the sacred offering as low
Devotion depends on proper regard
Improper regard undermines devotion
items.inference: For one who considers it low, devotion becomes vain.
items.plain_english: O great goddess, if one considers it low, that person's devotion is vain, utterly vain.

rows.grounds: compound indicating the supreme manner of seeing
totality of what is to be seen

items.question: In what manner should a devotee perceive all things without doubt?
premises: A devotee perceives all things
Perception can be shaped by spiritual understanding
Supreme vision removes doubt
items.inference: One should see all things in the highest, highest form without doubt.
items.plain_english: One should see everything in the highest, highest form, without doubt.

rows.grounds: locative absolute-like condition of spiritual realization
compound: social or ritual boundary of class

items.question: How can class boundaries be violated when supreme realization is present?
premises: Class boundaries ordinarily regulate conduct
Supreme realization transforms perception
A tension arises between realization and boundaries
items.inference: When such realization is present, class boundaries are not truly violated.
items.plain_english: When this is realized, how could the boundary of class be violated?

rows.grounds: compound: falling away from class position

items.question: What consequence follows from acting contrary to proper class conduct?
premises: One may act contrary to proper conduct
Class standing depends on proper conduct
Improper conduct has consequences
items.inference: One who acts otherwise incurs loss of class standing.
items.plain_english: But one who acts otherwise indeed incurs loss of class standing.

rows.grounds: fused form linking devotion and liberation

items.question: What spiritual result is bestowed by devotion that is complete, firm, and pure?
premises: Devotion can be complete, firm, and pure

Liberation is a supreme spiritual goal
items.inference: Complete, firm, and pure devotion bestows liberation.
items.plain_english: Devotion that is complete, firm, and pure bestows liberation.

rows.grounds: compound: attainment of a spiritual level

items.question: What lesser spiritual attainment may occur at the end for incomplete devotion?
premises: Spiritual attainment can vary in degree
The end state reflects the quality of practice
A lower attainment is possible
items.inference: At the end, a lower attainment of state may occur.
items.plain_english: O beautiful one in all limbs, at the end there may be attainment of a lower state.

rows.grounds: compound referring to duties of class and life-stage

items.question: Is observance of class and life-stage duties considered spiritually fruitful?

Observance of duties can have results
Tradition evaluates their fruitfulness
items.inference: Observance of the duties of class and life-stage is declared fruitful.
items.plain_english: Observance of the duties of class and stage of life is declared to be fruitful.

items.question: What title and position does this chapter on rules hold in the text?
premises: The section gives instruction on rules
Chapters are named and numbered
This is the concluding designation

items.plain_english: This is the ninth chapter, named the instruction on rules.
